screening_decisions.reason: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial of oral inosiplex in alopecia totalis assessing hair regrowth—meets RCT intervention criteria.
Parallel-group randomized, placebo-controlled trial of weekly oral prednisolone in extensive alopecia areata—eligible RCT.
Prospective randomized controlled, investigator-blinded comparison of two topical corticosteroid formulations in mild-to-moderate AA—eligible RCT.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of topical minoxidil vs placebo in extensive AA/AT/AU—eligible RCT.
Randomized double-blind regimen with minoxidil vs placebo (with subsequent switch) in extensive AA—eligible RCT.
Within-patient randomized double-blind comparison (DPCP + minoxidil vs DPCP + vehicle) with clinical outcomes—eligible RCT.
Patients with AT/AU nonresponders randomly assigned to cyclosporine, PUVA, or thymopentin; interventional comparison—eligible RCT.
Small within-subject ALA photodynamic therapy vs vehicle applied to different scalp areas in 6 patients without randomization—does not meet RCT criterion.
Randomized comparison of topical cyclosporin A vs vehicle in refractory AA—eligible RCT.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of imipramine for AA—eligible RCT.
Randomized assignment to topical immunotherapy (squaric acid dibutylester), interferon-α, or their combination with predefined response scale—eligible RCT.
Double-blind cyclosporin A vs placebo study in AA; design implies randomized, controlled evaluation—treated as RCT.
Randomized, double-blind, right–left, placebo-controlled clobetasol foam trial in AA—eligible RCT.
Randomized controlled post-steroid maintenance trial of topical minoxidil vs vehicle in AA—eligible RCT.
Report includes a double-blind, placebo-controlled minoxidil trial component with comparative outcomes in AA—treated as RCT.
Controlled comparative trial of squaric acid dibutylester, diphencyprone, minoxidil, and placebo in patchy AA; randomization not explicit—provisionally include.
Questionnaire-based survey of illness perceptions; noninterventional and not randomized—exclude.
Methodological commentary on when RCTs are unnecessary; not an interventional AA trial—exclude.
Randomized, double-blind, controlled aromatherapy (essential oils) vs carrier oils in AA with blinded outcome assessment—eligible RCT.
Narrative clinical update/review article; not a randomized controlled trial—exclude.
Retrospective population-based incidence/natural history study; no intervention or randomization—exclude.
Open prognostic analysis of DPCP-treated patients; no random allocation or control—exclude.
Comparative groups matched but not randomized (inosine pranobex and diphencyprone); nonrandomized study—exclude.
Genetic review; not an interventional randomized study—exclude.
Methods paper on assessing trial quality; not an RCT of AA treatment—exclude.
